terra.problem: David asks God to answer him before recalling that God relieved his distress. He does not thank God in this verse.
The verse says the men love vanity and seek lies; it does not say they do not love truth.
Keeping his mustache out of it has no clear connection to the command about anger, so the joke does not make sense.
Trust is not the last word of the verse; LORD is.
The oven filing a complaint does not make a clear comparison to a person fasting.
The verse does not mention only trusting the LORD; it also commands offering sacrifices of the righteous.
The claim that many Israelites made trips to Jerusalem is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The verse says many ask the question. It does not say a crowd is gathered or that they keep asking.
The verse says many ask the question, but does not say they are a gathered crowd.
The verse compares David's joy with a time when grain and new wine abound; it does not identify that time as harvest.
The verse speaks of grain and new wine abounding, not specifically of the joy a harvest brings.
The pillow joke follows the statement that David's peace rests on the LORD, making the LORD the object of the comparison.
